record.context_brief: complete affine structures on surface-times-circle manifolds
record.original_question: Conjecture: for every closed surface Σ_g with g ≥ 2, the product manifold Σ_g × S^1 does not admit any complete affine structure.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.15. The manifold \(\Sigma_{g\geq 2}\times \mathbf{S}^1\) does not admit any complete affine structure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_g$ denote a closed orientable surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $S^1$ denote the circle. A complete affine structure on a smooth manifold $M^n$ is an atlas of charts into $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of $\mathbb{R}^n$, such that the developing map $\widetilde{M} \to \mathbb{R}^n$ is a diffeomorphism (equivalently, $M$ is affinely diffeomorphic to a quotient $\mathbb{R}^n/\Gamma$ where $\Gamma$ is a discrete subgroup of the affine group $\mathrm{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ acting properly discontinuously and freely on $\mathbb{R}^n$).

Prove or disprove: for every integer $g \geq 2$, the closed 3-manifold $\Sigma_g \times S^1$ admits no complete affine structure.
artifact.status_search_result: Closed 3-manifolds admitting complete affine structures were classified by Fried and Goldman: such a manifold must be finitely covered by a 2-torus bundle over the circle (i.e., its geometry is Euclidean, Nil, or Sol). Since $\Sigma_g \times S^1$ for $g \geq 2$ has a fundamental group that is not virtually polycyclic, it does not appear in this classification, so it cannot admit a complete affine structure. The conjecture therefore follows from the Fried–Goldman classification.

status_evidence.title: Complete affine 3-manifolds and hyperbolic surfaces (Goldman)
status_evidence.snippet: A closed 3-manifold admits a complete affine structure if and only if it is finitely covered by a 2-torus bundle over the circle; in other words, it is Euclidean, Heisenberg, or Sol.
status_evidence.claim: Closed 3-manifolds with complete affine structures are classified by Fried–Goldman, ruling out $\Sigma_g\times S^1$ for $g\geq 2$.

status_evidence.title: Three-Dimensional Affine Crystallographic Groups (Fried–Goldman)
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of compact complete affine 3-manifolds via affine crystallographic groups.
status_evidence.claim: Fried–Goldman classified compact complete affine 3-manifolds; their fundamental groups are virtually polycyclic.
